comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @bigd4 for the MR (while it has opened 4 years ago)! I confirmed the issue still exists in the present master. I have now rebased the MR, while I take essentially the same approach as yours. The major change is that, since `PSTRESS` is always found in `vasprun.xml` in the `parameters/ionic` section, I now rely on it (rather than the `incar` section, where `PSTRESS` exists only when users specify it explicitly in `INCAR`), which can avoid an additional if statement.

I have tested the MR with the attached sample VASP calculations for C ([2685.zip](/uploads/80d6d7879bf2dc46e08967234f0d698c/2685.zip)). Before the MR, we obtain
```
force_consistent = False
read_vasp_out: -20.24720095
read_vasp_xml: -20.24010135
diff         : 0.007099600000000095
force_consistent = True
read_vasp_out: -20.24695937
read_vasp_xml: -20.23985977
diff         : 0.007099600000000095
```
while after the MR, the energy values are essentially the same as those in OUTCAR as
```
force_consistent = False
read_vasp_out: -20.24720095
read_vasp_xml: -20.247200953169394
diff         : -3.169393636426321e-09
force_consistent = True
read_vasp_out: -20.24695937
read_vasp_xml: -20.246959373169393
diff         : -3.169393636426321e-09
```
I now also added a test based on the above results and would like to merge.
